evidence.section: 3.1 Primary MC carbide in the heat-treated alloys
evidence.quote: The primary MC presents an irregularly blocky morphology, regardless of the compositions of alloys ( Table 1 ). Its volume fraction is about 1.2 – 1.3%

evidence.section: 3.1 Primary MC carbide in the heat-treated alloys
evidence.quote: The microstructures of investigated alloys after the heat treatment are mostly composed of γ matrix, γ’ phase, primary MC and secondary carbides (M23C6 or M6C).

evidence.section: 3.1 Primary MC carbide in the heat-treated alloys
evidence.quote: The microstructures of investigated alloys after the heat treatment are mostly composed of γ matrix, γ’ phase, primary MC and secondary carbides (M23C6 or M6C).
The A0 - A4 alloys have a big (Mo + W)/Cr ratio approaching that of K446 alloy and hence the primary MC in these alloys tends to decompose into the M6C carbide ( Fig. 4 (a)- 4 (e)).
in the A5, A7 and A8 alloys the M6C carbide initially forms and is gradually replaced by the M23C6 carbide with the reduction of the (Mo + W)/Cr ratio from 1.07 to 0.22 ( Fig. 4 (f)- 4 (i)).
the η phase forms owing to the high (Nb + Ti)/Al ratio as well as the high Dt value when the primary MC decomposes in the A4, A7 and A8 alloys

The Nv values of A1 and A6 alloys (2.47 and 2.92) are within or beyond the critical range of σ phase precipitation, respectively ( Table 1 ); hence, the σ phase occurs in the two alloys during thermal exposure ( Figs. 10 and 11 ).
the μ phase heavily precipitates in the A5 alloy
restrain the precipitation of topologically close-packed (TCP) phases and promote the coarsening of grain boundaries (GBs)
there exists an interfacial transition layer at the edge of primary MC, the contrast of which is grayer than that of the near-center zone of the carbide

attributes.location: reaction region of primary MC decomposition

evidence.quote: The multi-layer microstructure like the MC/M23C6/ γ’ / γ in the magnified image of the “ Area 2 ” in Fig. 5 (a) often occurs in the reaction region of primary MC decomposition
The STEM observations with the EDS analyses show that primary MC decomposition is an inter-diffusion process of elements between the primary MC carbide and γ matrix
the concentration gradients of various elements between the primary MC and γ matrix are the main driving force for the primary MC decomposition at elevated temperatures
